title: Late-shift ops pocket docket — console triage & followups
content:
(scratchpad) Late shift notes, mostly for myself — keep concise.

22:05 — quick summary
- Customer email (acct: tilecraft) reports dashboard widgets returning 502s intermittently.
- Repro on EU region, node pool: ded-gpu-01. Error spikes coincide with a burst of short chat gen requests.
- Temporary mitigation: route tilecraft to lower-throughput token bucket (policy id: TB-98) until followup.

22:15 — checks run
- Pulled logs from ded-gpu-01 (last 6h) -> saw KV cache evictions + OOM spikes at 21:58 and 22:08.
- Observed increased continuous-batching batches (batch size up to 48) for short seq len (avg 18 tokens).
- CPU on control-plane ~35% steady, but GPU memory climbs past expected for quantized model variant.

Quick experiment tried
- bumped per-model max-batch to 24 for model redwood/fastchat-13b-q4 to test (ran on staging first).
- Curl to toggle route (staging) — example:
  curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/routes/route123/tweak \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    -d '{"max_batch":24}'
  (note: must use real route id in prod)

Unresolved notes
- Is the autoscaler kicking in fast enough for many short requests? config: autoscale.policy.v2 -> cooldown 180s. Maybe reduce to 60s for bursty chat routes. Need perf/runbook change request.
- Need to confirm whether quantized kernels for this model have regression on this hardware (A100-v4 in EU). Tagging research/ops.

Customer follow-ups (short messages)
- Send templated update to tilecraft: "We've throttled your route to reduce errors while we investigate; will update in 2h or sooner."
- Offer schedule for a replay window if they want logs. Attach incident id JIRA-4827.

22:40 — quick todo before handoff
- Add short note to oncall board with mitigation + next steps.
- Open small perf investigation PR to test lowering cooldown in canary (PR drafted).
- Check if fallback to hosted-lower-tier model (faster but lower quality) would be acceptable for tilecraft as a fallback option.

Random scratch ideas
- If short-seq heavy workloads cause large batches -> maybe bias batcher to cap batch-size for seq<32. Could add heuristic: if avg_seq_len < 32 and rps_peak>200 -> cap batch at 24.
- Cache keys: prefix caching seems not to be used by this customer (dynamic prompts), but KV eviction pattern shows potential for LRU mis-tuning.

Notes to self next shift
- Validate PR #1298 <> runtime kernel selection logs. Confirm table of kernel choices for redwood/fastchat-13b-q4 on A100-v4.
- Run synthetic load on staging, mimic tilecraft payload (many short prompts in parallel) and run memory profiler.
- If safe, plan controlled rollout of max_batch change and autoscale cooldown change behind a feature flag.

End-of-shift handoff summary (short)
- What I did: applied per-model max_batch tweak on staging, routed tilecraft to token-bucket TB-98 in prod, left short note in Slack.
- Open actions: performance PR, kernel regression check, customer update scheduled at +2h.
- Blockers: need research confirmation on kernel regression.

Misc quick logs (for search later)
- observed log lines: "kv_cache: evict key=ctx_... size=120MB" at 21:58
- error hit: "runtime: OutOfMemoryError: device 0" repeated 14x
- candidate jira entries: JIRA-4827 (tilecraft 502s), JIRA-4832 (batcher tuning)

End of scratchpad. Keep succinct in handoff.
todo_items: Draft customer update message for tilecraft and post (assign Priya to review)
Create perf investigation PR (link to draft in linked_artifacts)
Run synthetic short-seq load on staging and capture memory flamegraphs
Confirm kernel selection table for fastchat-13b-q4 on A100-v4 with research
Add heuristic to batcher config proposal (cap on short-seq burst batches)
